old_caption:
The video captures a nighttime scene featuring a house adorned with festive Christmas lights. The focal point is a large, illuminated Christmas tree positioned in the front yard. The tree is decorated with colorful lights, including white, purple, green, and yellow, arranged to form a smiling face with eyes and a mouth. At the top of the tree, a bright star shines prominently. Surrounding the tree, the roof of the house is decorated with snowflake patterns in green and white lights, adding to the holiday ambiance.

To the right of the tree, a red neon sign reads "TUNE TO FM 67.3," suggesting a local radio station promotion. The house itself has a simple design with a light-colored exterior and a dark roof. A small garden area with some plants and a pathway leading up to the entrance is visible in the foreground. On the left side of the frame, part of a parked car is seen, indicating the presence of a driveway.

Throughout the video, the lighting on the tree's face animates, shifting between expressions such as a smile and a more neutral look, while the star and snowflake lights remain static.

caption:
The video captures a nighttime residential front yard dominated by a tall cone-shaped LED Christmas-tree display crowned by a glowing star, its pixelated surface showing two eyes with eyebrows and a pink nose above a green-and-yellow striped base. Behind it a single-story house carries a red illuminated sign, while several snowflake lights glow in the dark above the roofline. A parked car sits at left and a thin cable slants across the dark sky, with the camera holding steady.

The visible motion is mainly the animated on-tree face. The mouth of the pixel face, already animating on the first frame, cycles shape after shape. A closed grin alternates with a grin showing white teeth against a dark mouth and a grin with a red tongue protruding. Occasional wide-open dark O forms suggest a singing expression. The eyes, eyebrows, nose, star, striped base, house, red sign, parked car and snowflake lights appear fixed, making the animated mouth the clearest changing element.

The mouth animation continues without pause.

a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
